newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello says budget cuts less than last time.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello says budget cuts less than last time.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday that savings in the coming May budget would not be as large as those in the last budget in August.
"What it's saying is we'll have (savings) next time around but nothing of the dimensions of last time," Costello told Perth Radio 6PR.
The Liberal-National government budgeted for 1996/97 (June 30) savings of A$7.2 billion in its August budget, but this was reduced to A$6.8 billion after the Senate knocked back some measures.

Costello said on Tuesday he would not look for sufficient savings to balance the government's finances next financial year, which according to forward estimates would require a fiscal tightening of A$4 billion.
Costello on Tuesday announced a revised forecast for the 1996/97 underlying budget deficit of A$8.49 billion, compared with the A$5.65 billion projected in the August budget.
The revised forecast was issued as part of the government's regular mid-year review of budget projections.
The underlying budget deficit excludes items such as asset sales and early repayment of debt by the states.
